h: A neighbourhood picture house in north Bristol
p: The Orpheus is a proper local cinema, the kind of place that regulars talk about with real fondness. It sits in the leafy residential streets of Westbury Park and Henleaze, away from the city-centre bustle, so it suits anyone who'd rather avoid the crowds of the big multiplexes and enjoy a film somewhere a bit more personal.

Because the venue has a lot of steps and no wheelchair access, it's worth being honest with your group before booking. If anyone can't manage stairs, Bristol's city-centre cinemas will be a better fit for that trip, and you can save the Orpheus for a night when everyone can get in comfortably.
Getting there and making a night of it

With no car park of its own, local buses are a good option, and the area is easy to reach from Whiteladies Road and the Gloucester Road side of the city. If you do drive, leave yourself plenty of time to find legal on-street parking, read the signs carefully and steer well clear of the supermarket car park next door.

The Downs are close by, a huge open stretch of grassland where you can stroll, kick a ball about or fly a kite before the film. Walk across towards Clifton and you'll reach the edge of the Avon Gorge, with views down to the river and across to the Clifton Suspension Bridge, one of Bristol's great sights. It's a cracking walk on a bright evening, and Clifton Village has cafés and pubs to round things off.

Henleaze Road and the surrounding streets have independent shops and places to eat, so it's easy to grab a bite before the screening. For families, a weekend matinee followed by a run around on the Downs is a lovely low-key afternoon.

It's a smaller venue, so popular new releases and evening showings can sell out. Book in advance where you can, and check the screen details if anyone in your group needs hearing assistance or audio description, as the cinema can help with both if you ask.
Whether it's a midweek date or a family treat, the Orpheus is a reminder of how nice a neighbourhood cinema can feel.
